public_rationale: Contemporary records place public driverless service in a small number of metropolitan areas, with Austin's new service restricted to 37 square miles. That supports the ordinary geographic reading that most US places lacked access. Nissan's 2013 announcement establishes ambitious commitments more than a decade earlier. Working services did exist, which Marcus's wording allows.
limitations: Geographic coverage is assessed qualitatively rather than through a national area or population calculation.
This does not assess whether the operating services were safe, profitable, or technologically disappointing.
News reporting supplements operator disclosures because no comprehensive contemporary primary inventory was obtained.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Most parts of the US still lack functioning driverless car systems after more than a decade of lavish promises.

statement.excerpt: Most parts of the US still don’t have functioning driverless cars systems, for example, even after over a decade of lavish promises.
statement.document_title: Ezra Klein’s new take on AGI – and why I think it’s probably wrong

from_speaker: still don’t have functioning driverless cars systems
over a decade of lavish promises
our_interpretation: The ordinary reading concerns geographic availability of working driverless passenger services, without an onboard safety driver. It does not deny that services work in some cities.
For the ongoing state, use the latest publicly reportable month-to-date period before publication: March 1–5, 2025.
Read 'most parts' as most US places lacking access, rather than requiring a particular population or land-area denominator.
Read 'lavish promises' as ambitious public commitments. The adjective is evaluative; the existence and age of commitments are checkable.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporary deployment records show services confined to a small number of local areas, leaving most US places unserved, and historical records establish ambitious commitments more than ten years earlier.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Contemporary records show functioning driverless passenger services broadly available across most US places, or the claimed history of commitments is disproved.

evidence.excerpt: Waymo is now trying to expand into more cities

evidence.explanation: The article identifies existing Waymo service in Phoenix, San Francisco and Los Angeles, with Austin launching and other cities still planned. This supports geographically limited availability; national breadth is an inference from the deployment account.
Even the new Austin deployment served a bounded part of one city. It illustrates the distinction between a functioning service and widespread geographic availability.
